content: If you are allergic to conjugated estrogens, bazedoxifene, or any other substances, inform your doctor or pharmacist before taking this medication. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Avoid smoking or using tobacco while on this medication. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery, are planning to have surgery, or will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight), as these conditions can increase your risk of developing blood clots, especially when taking estrogen products. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses while on this medication. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. Estrogens can pass into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. It is unknown if bazedoxifene passes into breast milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test, blood clotting tests, thyroid tests), potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g. Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-examinations and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help. Engage in mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving crossword puzzles) to help prevent dementia. To promote healthy bones, increase weight-bearing exercises, quit smoking, limit alcohol intake, and consume a well-balanced diet with adequate calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Once the foil pouch is opened, the U.S. product expires after 60 days, and the Canadian product expires after 45 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Estrogens, whether used alone or with another hormone (progestin), have rarely caused very serious side effects. Discuss the risks and benefits of hormone treatment with your doctor. Estrogens can increase the risk of uterine cancer (endometrial cancer). However, the bazedoxifene in this product may help reduce this risk. In postmenopausal women, estrogens, with or without progestin, may increase the risk of breast/ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The risk of serious side effects may depend on the dose of estrogen and the duration of use. This medication should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest duration necessary. Regularly discuss the use of this medication with your doctor and check in every 3 to 6 months to determine if continued use is necessary.g., annually) as directed by your doctor.
